title: Fast-pass runway for low-bandwidth air-gapped enterprise upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: A set of regulated enterprise customers are reporting multi-week delays for private/Dedicated upgrades due to constrained outbound connectivity, strict cryptographic approval windows, and limited maintenance bandwidth on site. Current intake funnels treat these requests as generic 'airgap' tickets which creates bottlenecks in sequencing, risk acceptance, and comms.

Goal: Create a deterministic, lightweight 'fast-pass runway' that allows PMs and Solutions Engineers to triage low-bandwidth air-gapped upgrade requests quickly, identify minimum viable preflight artifacts, and coordinate a small set of engineering and legal checks to reduce total lead time from weeks to days while preserving security posture.

Scope: This ticket covers intake rubric, staging checklist, required artifacts, communication templates, initial engineering constraints (network probes and bundle delivery options), legal/KMS gating checklist, and an escalation flow. It does NOT cover automatic tooling to perform staged upgrades or any code changes to the runtime; follow-on engineering tickets will be created for automation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page intake rubric that can categorize requests into Fast-pass / Standard / Blocked lanes based on bandwidth, approval SLA, and cryptographic module constraints.
- A staged artifact checklist that lists the absolute minimum telemetry/packaging required to validate an upgrade in an air-gapped environment (signed bundle digest, per-node upgrade manifest, signed operator checklist).
- A 4-step comms template for SEs to send to customers (preflight probe, bundle transfer options, approval window, rollback triggers).
- Engineering runbook stub that defines two supported bundle delivery mechanisms (offline USB bundle with signed manifest OR ephemeral pull via single-connection proxy) and required network probe results.
- Legal/KMS gating checklist that identifies which customers need HSM attestation and which can use sealed symmetric keys for short-lived upgrades.
- A measurable SLA target: reduce median intake-to-approved time from current baseline to <= 5 business days for Fast-pass candidates.

Stakeholders: PM (Marco Diaz), Solutions Eng (Nora Patel), Security (Ravi Menon), Legal (K. Alvarez), Runtime Eng (Sophie Chen), Support Ops (Luis Ortega).

Success metrics: time-to-approval, number of escalations to Product Security, customer satisfaction CSAT for onboarding, number of rework cycles in install window per customer.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Initial intake: Customer ACME Financial (support case SC-2026-7783) requests a scheduled upgrade but cannot accept outbound traffic beyond a single bastion during a 2-hour window. SE flagged as high priority due to regulatory audit next quarter.

2026-03-11 - SE review: Nora Patel ran network probe template (attached) and confirmed single-connection proxy possible, but customer legal requires HSM attestation for any remote signing. Recommend Fast-pass if HSM attestation is satisfied within 48 hours.

2026-03-11 - Security note: Ravi Menon: HSM attestation flow exists but needs explicit approval; proposed interim pattern: cryptographic escrow with signed offline bundle digest verified by on-prem operator. This reduces blast radius but will require a short policy exception for one customer. Added to gating checklist.

2026-03-12 - Engineering feasibility: Sophie Chen: runtime changes not required for manual bundle installs; however, we need an operator validation script (shell + Python shim) and a signed manifest verifier. Estimate 3 points; recommend separate ENG ticket for automation after pilot.

2026-03-12 - PM decision: Move to Planned. Assign Marco Diaz to own the intake rubric and comms templates. Create follow-on ENG ticket for operator validation tooling and a security review ticket for the HSM exception process. Draft comms templates to be shared with SEs for feedback.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: (1) Draft intake rubric and checklist, (2) Create two engineering tickets (operator-validator & ephemeral-proxy playbook), (3) Schedule 1-hour alignment with Security and Legal on 2026-03-15.
2026-03-12 - Linked customer artifacts: see linked_artifacts for support case and probe logs; SE to attach customer's cryptographic attestation once received.
notes_for_SEs: Use the intake checklist to capture exact acceptable channels and an operator contact. If customer cannot provide HSM attestation within 48 hours, route to Standard lane. For Fast-pass, get legal sign-off on the escrow exception before scheduling the upgrade window.
comm_plan: 1) SE sends preflight probe request (template), 2) Customer returns signed bundle digest + attestation, 3) Legal approves escrow exception if needed, 4) Schedule 2-hour maintenance window and run operator validation script. Post-upgrade: 72-hour monitoring with telemetry snapshot submission.
